title: Red Velvet Cupcakes with Cream Cheese Frosting
changes_from_base: Whisked oil-and-buttermilk batter with cocoa, vinegar and red colouring replaces the creamed butter cake; cream cheese frosting.
summary: Made in the same tin and oven as the classic vanilla cupcakes, but with a whisked oil-and-buttermilk batter tinted red and flavoured with cocoa and vinegar instead of a creamed butter cake. Topped with tangy cream cheese frosting.
equipment: 12-hole muffin tin lined with paper cases
stand mixer or electric hand whisk
piping bag with a large star nozzle

ingredients.item: cake flour (or plain flour; see note)
ingredients.note: plain flour works with a slightly firmer crumb

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
full-fat cream cheese (block), at room temperature
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: Heat the oven to 175°C (155°C fan) for at least 20 minutes with a shelf in the middle, and line the muffin tin with paper cases.

steps.title: Sift the dry mix
steps.text: Sift the flour, caster sugar, bicarbonate of soda, salt and cocoa into one of the large bowls. Sifting removes lumps of cocoa and spreads the bicarbonate evenly so every cake rises the same.

steps.title: Whisk the wet mix
steps.text: In the other bowl, whisk the oil, buttermilk, egg, yolk, colouring, vinegar and vanilla until evenly coloured. Oil keeps the crumb moist and soft, even straight from the fridge.

steps.title: Combine and fill
steps.text: Add the dry mix to the wet and whisk just until smooth. The buttermilk and vinegar start reacting with the bicarbonate straight away, so fill the cases about two-thirds full and get them into the oven promptly.

steps.title: Bake and cool
steps.text: Bake for 17-21 minutes until springy and a skewer comes out clean. Leave them in the tin for 5 minutes, then cool completely on the wire rack before frosting.

steps.title: Make the frosting
steps.text: Beat the butter until smooth, add the cream cheese and beat just until combined, then add the icing sugar, vanilla and salt and mix on low until smooth. Over-beating cream cheese breaks down its structure and makes the frosting runny. Chill for 15 minutes if it feels soft.

steps.title: Pipe and serve
steps.text: Pipe swirls of frosting onto the cold cupcakes using the star nozzle and keep them chilled. Take them out 20 minutes before serving so the frosting softens and the flavour comes through.

tips: Add the red colouring a little at a time and stir well; gel colours are strong, and a few drops give a deep red without any bitter taste.
A common mistake is frosting warm cupcakes; the cream cheese frosting melts and slides off, so wait until they are completely cold.
Use natural cocoa, not Dutch-processed, as its acidity helps the rise and the soft red colour.
Check that the gel colouring is carmine-free.
Use block cream cheese rather than spreadable tubs, which make a looser frosting.
safety: Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Because of the cream cheese frosting, keep the cupcakes in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days. Unfrosted cupcakes freeze for up to 2 months; thaw at room temperature before frosting.
